$comment: Align the Top GND pour with the board, and with the other three zones.
Spotted by eye in the PCB editor and confirmed to predate all of this work --
the offset is byte-identical in 52586d4, the original EasyEDA import. The
Bottom GND, Inner1 GND and Inner2 +5V zones are all the same 76-point rounded
rectangle inset 0.13 mm from the board edge on every side. The Top GND zone is
that same shape translated by (+0.867, -2.539) mm, which is not a clearance
and not a shape difference -- just a displacement.
What it costs: the pour overhangs the top and right edges, where the fill
clips it away harmlessly, and falls SHORT along the bottom by 2.67 mm and the
left by 0.99 mm -- strips of board with no top-layer ground. Inner1 still
covers the whole board, so this is shielding and copper balance rather than
connectivity, which is why nothing flagged it: DRC has no opinion about where
Moving it by the inverse puts all four zones on the same rectangle.
